title: Corduroy wales from pinwale to wide wale
purpose: Generate tileable PBR maps of corduroy: rounded cut-pile wales running down the tile, grooves showing the ground weave, pile grain and lustre, crushed worn tops, and thick-and-thin wales. Use for trousers, jackets, upholstery, cushions and soft furnishings.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python corduroy_wales.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: wales
parameters.meaning: Wales across the tile width: about 40 is pinwale or needlecord, 6 is wide wale; rounded up to an even count when wales alternate.

parameters.name: groove
parameters.meaning: Width of the groove between wales as a share of the wale spacing.

parameters.name: pile
parameters.meaning: Strength of the cut-pile grain on the cords.

parameters.name: sheen
parameters.meaning: Lustre of the pile on the cord tops.

parameters.name: wear
parameters.meaning: Crushed, lighter cord tops in patches.

parameters.name: alternate
parameters.meaning: Thick-and-thin corduroy: how much wider every other wale is than its neighbour.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: pinwale_navy
presets.description: Navy pinwale (needlecord) with fine, shallow grooves.

presets.name: wide_wale_rust
presets.description: Rust wide-wale corduroy with worn, crushed cords.

presets.name: thick_thin_olive
presets.description: Olive thick-and-thin corduroy: wide and narrow wales alternate.

presets.name: lustre_burgundy
presets.description: Burgundy lustrous needlecord with a velvet sheen.

limits: Wales are rounded height profiles with fibre noise, not modelled tufts; the pile lean shows as tone and roughness, so the directional sheen of real corduroy (which changes with view angle) is only approximated. Wales run along V only; rotate the UVs for horizontal cords. Wear is noise-driven, not placed at knees or elbows. The groove weave fades out where it would be finer than a few pixels. Occlusion is a blurred-height estimate, not ray traced.
technique_references: Wale layout per pixel column with whole wale counts
Rounded cord profile with power-shaped falloff
Anisotropic fractal noise for pile grain and lean streaks
Cosine weft ridges in the grooves
Height to tangent-space normal by central differences
